text.p: Spanish championship matches scheduled for the weekend (league standings in parentheses, all kick-off times gmt):
Tenerife (7) v Athletic Bilbao (8) ko 2100 gmt
Athletic will be without suspended defender Aitor Lizarazu for a game that has been brought forward to an unusual Friday slot because of Tenerife's UEFA Cup match at Brondby on Tuesday.
Atletico miss suspended Argentine internationals Diego Simeone and Juan Eduardo Esnaider and may feel the effects of their heroic 5-4 midweek cup defeat by Barcelona.
Espanyol went down in the cup to second division Las Palmas on Wednesday and may struggle to gain a result against a Deportivo side that is yet to lose under new coach Carlos Alberto Silva.

Sporting coach Benito Floro will have to find a replacement for suspended defender David Cano against a Sevilla side that is looking ever more likely to be relegated to the second division for the first time in 25 years.
Valladolid coach Vicente Cantatore is expected to remodel his midfield after seeing his side's bid for a UEFA Cup place run out of steam in recent weeks.

Striker Pineda and defender Juanito return after suspension for an Extremadura side that won their first game in the top flight against Zaragoza earlier this season and have been in good form in recent weeks. Zaragoza will be without suspended Argentine defender Kily Gonzalez.
This mid-table clash is a re-run of their cup game being played in Celta on Thursday.

Oviedo will have to find replacements for Russian midfielder Viktor Onopko and Portuguese defender Paulo Bento, who are on international duty, against a side that has always looked likely to go straight back to the second division.

Another game between two sides set to meet each other in the cup on Thursday, in which the notoriously boggy Rayo pitch may again be the biggest enemy for the team with the best away record in the league.

Former Atletico Madrid defender Ivan Rocha is set to return for Logrones against a Barcelona team that will call upon strength in depth after Thursday's exhausting 5-4 cup win over Atletico. Barcelona beat Logrones 8-0 earlier this season.

Real Madrid came back from an early goal to beat the Basque side 6-1 in October and are looking increasingly likely champions. It is the third consecutive Monday fixture for the leaders, who are still without injured striker Emilio Amavisca.
